fields.title: Proposition de loi visant à encadrer l’implantation des centres de données sur le territoire français (Senate first reading)
fields.principles: CURATOR: assign (candidates: local siting say, water)
key_terms: la publication du décret qualifiant un projet de centre de données de projet d’intérêt national majeur est subordonnée à l’organisation préalable
fields.key_terms_translation: EN machine: The publication of the decree qualifying a data-centre project as a major national-interest project is conditional on a prior project committee, organised by the developer at its own cost, with the State representative, the host commune, neighbouring communes and intercommunal bodies.
fields.summary: The Senate adopted at first reading a bill under which a data centre can be qualified as a major national-interest project only after the developer convenes, at its own cost, a project committee with the State, the host commune, neighbouring communes and intercommunal bodies. It also lets the administration refuse a construction permit where water resources are structurally stressed. Passed by the Senate only; not yet law.
fields.source_title: Sénat, texte adopté n° 73 (25 March 2026), proposition de loi visant à encadrer l’implantation des centres de données

records.verbatim: la publication du décret qualifiant un projet de centre de données de projet d’intérêt national majeur est subordonnée à l’organisation préalable
records.notes: Passed Senate first reading only, so status proposed. Water-stress refusal clause is in the same article. Verified by pdftext containment.

fields.title: Route for very large data centres into the NSIP consenting regime (AI Growth Zones policy paper)
key_terms: However, a small number of very large projects may need to go through the Nationally Significant Infrastructure Projects
fields.summary: The government's AI Growth Zones policy paper (published 13 November 2025) says most AI data centres will be consented through the standard local planning process, while a small number of very large projects may go through the NSIP consenting route. It says a National Policy Statement for Data Centres will set the thresholds.
fields.source_title: GOV.UK: Delivering AI Growth Zones (13 Nov 2025)

records.verbatim: However, a small number of very large projects may need to go through the Nationally Significant Infrastructure Projects
records.notes: Same URL as seed record gb-ai-growth-zones-2025 but a different instrument (the DCO route, not the zone designations). Status left proposed: the commencement date secondary sources give (8 Jan 2026) is not verified on legislation.gov.uk. Verified by probe.

fields.summary: Utsunomiya City's solicitation (dated 30 April 2026) selects a private data-centre developer for city-marketed land beside the Shin-Tochigi substation, which the city describes as able to supply large amounts of power relatively early.
